reasoning: The extract gives fairly concrete success measures: "reductions in the sales weighted average sugar content per 100 grams", "reductions in portion size", or "a clear sales shift towards lower sugar alternatives". It also sets out an evaluation plan with a timetable. PHE will "publish interim reports on progress every 6 months", and will give an assessment "at 18 and 36 months (September 2018 and March 2020)", using "analysis of sales data and food composition data". It says what happens to the results: Government "will use this information to determine whether sufficient progress is being made" and will use other levers if there is not "sufficient progress by 2020". An Ofsted thematic review in 2017 is also planned, and it will provide "examples of good practice and recommendations". This clearly reaches level 2, with success measures, evaluation plans and a timetable. It comes close to level 3 because it includes publication of interim reports and a decision point. The strongest counter-example to level 3 is that the extract never explains why this evaluation design was chosen, or why testing before rollout is or is not appropriate. It also does not define "sufficient progress" or say which thresholds would trigger other levers. The line "These interventions will measure changes in purchasing behaviour and the impact on revenue" is vague. There is no mention of piloting or consultation. To reach level 3 the document would need to justify its evaluation approach, say whether the policy was tested first, define what counts as sufficient progress, and make clear that the assessments themselves will be published.
